correctness.rationale: For any iid spatial-reset distribution supported on a compact positive interval, the killed Brownian hitting-time transform proves a finite absorption mean \( (1-s_0)/(rs) \). The competing zero-hit, upper-threshold-hit and reset equations \(Df''=rf\) give exact hyperbolic-sine expressions; a regenerative first-cycle argument yields \(\Pr(M\ge m)=t(1-s_0)(u+s/s_0)/[(1-t)(s+tu)]\). Its derivative with respect to the positive exponential moment is strictly positive when the threshold exceeds the initial point and reset support. For \(Y=e^{-kZ}\), strict Jensen and secant-line inequalities give \(u_{\min}=1/s\) and the unique upper two-endpoint extremizer. Mixtures attain the full interval; the positive exponential moment is invertible from one exceedance probability. All quantifiers, strictness and degenerate fixed-mean cases are handled. The standalone checker passed 8,276 formula and stochastic diagnostics, not substituted for the universal proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The fixed-mean constraint is equivalent to fixing the negative exponential reset-location moment \(s=\mathbb E[e^{-kZ}]\), but the above-support path maximum solves a doubly killed interval problem and depends additionally on the positive exponential moment \(u=\mathbb E[e^{kZ}]\). value.rationale: The pre-absorption path maximum is a physically motivated search-risk observable independent of merely minimizing mean completion time. The full attainable excursion-probability interval and simultaneous threshold order, with unique deterministic and endpoint-mixture extremizers, characterize an exact global design tradeoff at fixed search efficiency. A single extreme-event measurement recovers an otherwise hidden exponential reset-location moment. The illustrative equal-mean policies have exact risk 0.5 versus approximately 0.344453 at threshold 4, a substantial difference. This is a complete natural optimization classification, not an arbitrary finite calculation or numeric table.
